title: Adaptation across an extreme elevational gradient in Andean leaf-eared mice; the world's highest-dwelling mammal.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed all 76 files in the FigShare deposit via its application programming interface (licence CC BY 4.0) and downloaded and opened all 7 physiology spreadsheets with pandas: BMR.xlsx 42 rows, P50.xlsx 20, SaO2.xlsx 96, VO2max_RelVO2_AS.xlsx 114 (about 38 mice x 3 oxygen levels), enzyme/mitochondrial-respiration 36 rows per tissue x 4 tissues, Hematological_variables_and_CA_activity 25, Liver GST 31. Confirmed the deposit holds only scripts plus three genome-annotation files (toga_final_annotation.gtf 153 MB, maker_annotation.gff 81 MB, toga_raw.bed 12 MB) and NO genotype matrix, VCF (variant call format) file, dosage array or allele-frequency table. Confirmed PRJNA950396 has 308 Sequence Read Archive runs (raw reads only). Read the full methods and data-availability text from the PubMed Central article page.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Sample sizes I could not open directly: 167 P. vaccarum whole genomes from 33 localities (data S1), 40 liver RNA-sequencing samples (table S3), 13 highland plus lowland mice in the common-garden physiology experiment. Supplementary data S1-S5 were not retrievable: Europe PMC returned 'Article with id PMC13595044 is not open access', and the PubMed Central /bin/ download path is blocked.

a1_downloadable.note: FigShare deposit (CC BY 4.0) downloaded without login; physiology spreadsheets and annotation files all opened. But the data-availability statement promises 'raw genotype and physiological data' and the genotype part is simply absent from the deposit.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Physiological labels are real columns with units: vo2 and vo2nor in VO2max_RelVO2_AS.xlsx, BMR, P50, sao2, 'GST_activity (umol g tissue-1 min-1)'. Verified in the files.

a3_inputs_present.note: The only features in the downloadable tables are population label, elevation, sex and body mass. The genomic input exists solely as 308 raw-read runs in the Sequence Read Archive; no genotype, allele-frequency or dosage file was deposited, so any genotype-to-phenotype model would require re-calling variants from raw whole-genome reads (terabyte scale, barred by project policy and the 50 MB cap).

a4_units_stated.note: Units are in the column headers (nmol/mg*min for respiration, umol/g tissue*min for enzymes, mM CO2 for Km); the enzyme workbook also has a 'Definitions' sheet. Verified in the files.

a5_enough_rows.note: Largest table opened is 114 respirometry rows from roughly 38 individual mice; every other assay is 20-96 rows, mitochondrial respiration is 36 rows per tissue, liver RNA-sequencing is 40 samples, and the genomic cohort is 167 individuals. The unit of analysis is the mouse, so n is tens, against the checklist's floor of about 1,500 (400 for classification).

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~250 MB for the whole FigShare deposit; <1 MB for all physiology tables
a6_fits_laptop.note: The deposited tables are trivially small; the part that would not fit (raw reads, hundreds of gigabytes to terabytes) is also the part that is missing as processed data.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: File counts are consistent with the paper's stated group sizes (n = 6-15 per group, 13 highland mice): 36-row respirometry tissue sheets and 42-row basal-metabolic-rate table match. Could not cross-check the 167-genome count because data S1 was unretrievable.

a8_label_provenance.note: Physiological labels are direct lab measurements (flow-through respirometry, high-resolution respirometry, enzyme assays), not model outputs. Note the alternative genomic framing would fail here: PBE (population branch excess) and LFMM (latent factor mixed model) outlier status are statistics computed from the same genotypes, i.e. leakage by construction.

existing_models.name: diploS/HIC (convolutional neural network classifier of selective sweeps, 2018)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported as powerful at moderate-to-small sample sizes on simulated data; I read only the search-result summary and the G3 abstract listing, not the full paper.

existing_models.name: Flex-Sweep (machine-learning sweep detector, Molecular Biology and Evolution 2023)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported higher power and lower false-positive rate than diploS/HIC on simulated complete sweeps; from the search-result summary only.

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Not written: with tens of phenotyped mice and no deposited genotype table there is no feature/label table to join anything to.

controls.positive_control: Would have been the published highland-versus-lowland difference in thermogenic maximal oxygen consumption at 8.7% oxygen.
controls.external_validation: Storz-lab deer mouse (Peromyscus maniculatus) thermogenesis datasets exist but are separately published and not joinable here.

honest_claim_h3: At best: 'among roughly 38 common-garden mice from two Chilean populations, population of origin and body mass predict thermogenic oxygen consumption' - a t-test, not a model.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use whole-genome variation in wild Andean mice to predict their cold-and-low-oxygen heat-production capacity.
plain_idea.train_on: Intended input: per-individual genetic variants plus elevation of capture. Verified reality: only about 38 mice have respirometry, and no genotype table was deposited at all.
plain_idea.predict: Thermogenic maximal oxygen consumption measured by flow-through respirometry at 21%, 12% and 8.7% oxygen, plus mitochondrial respiration rates from high-resolution respirometry on permeabilized muscle.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Comparative physiologists studying high-altitude adaptation would want to know which genetic variants predict performance; even a null result would quantify how little genotype explains whole-animal performance. But the sample size makes this unanswerable from this paper.

more_or_better_data.why: Existing sweep detectors such as diploS/HIC and Flex-Sweep train on millions of simulated genomic windows; this paper contributes 167 low-coverage genomes of one species with no deposited genotype file.

confidence_score.why: With 6-15 mice per group there is no way to estimate per-prediction uncertainty beyond a group mean and standard error.

models_beatable.why: diploS/HIC is a 2018 convolutional network evaluated on simulations, so it is in principle improvable, but that is a simulation-based methods project that does not need this paper's data.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No baseline model takes this paper's inputs, the genotype features are not deposited, and no shared evaluation split exists.

ml_idea: Considered: predict thermogenic maximal oxygen consumption or mitochondrial respiratory capacity from individual genotype across the elevational gradient; alternatively predict which genes carry elevation-associated selection signals from sequence and expression features. The first dies on sample size (tens of mice), the second on label provenance (the selection statistic is computed from the same genotypes).

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: all physiology spreadsheets together are under 1 MB and opened in pandas in seconds; the annotation files total about 245 MB and were not downloaded (size read from the FigShare application programming interface).
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows in VO2max_RelVO2_AS.xlsx - 114 respirometry measurements on about 38 mice - and list the FigShare deposit to confirm no genotype file exists. Both take five minutes and both kill the project.

verdict_reason: Fails A5 and A3: the phenotype tables cover only tens of individual mice (114 respirometry rows, 42 basal-metabolic-rate rows, 40 liver RNA-sequencing samples) and the genotype features promised in the data-availability statement are not in the FigShare deposit, leaving only 308 raw-read runs in the Sequence Read Archive. Beautiful natural-history physiology, but a statistics-not-machine-learning dataset.
